results.interpretation: The gap text describes the earlier research-runtime receipt (allowance at 100%). The later paired acceptance on 2026-09-19 ran Astra then Claude as the two steps of the research-pair graph under Dagu 2.16.6. The native run record, replayed through the pinned dagu history/status CLI, shows both steps succeeded, and each step printed the worker result that the adoption receipt records (duration_ms 14953 and 10538). The full returned reports are retained with matching hashes. Complete returned results from model workers inside the orchestrated graph are therefore established by the adoption/paired record.

limits: No new model inference was run for this check (the only model call in this unit was the read-only Codex review): the Codex /status arm of the next_check was not executed because no new paired run was needed, the shared Claude account is reserved, and a new paired run would add native Claude/Codex hook observations to the live ai-memory store. The evidence is the 2026-09-19 native run, not a fresh one.

The dagu history/status output was produced by the pinned 2.16.6 binary against a byte-identical copy of the retained run record in a temp DAGU_HOME, not against the live service home, so the live service was not touched. It is a replay of the stored record, not a re-execution.
The step stdout records are the run_worker.py summaries (role, status, duration); the full reports are the hash-matched files under adoption/paired/.

The research-runtime README/receipt text that still says paired_model_workflow_executed false is historical and is superseded by its own "Later paired acceptance" pointer; the landscape ledger row was not edited (forbidden path).

Disclosure (fix round 4, second independent review): this unit did make contact with the live ai-memory service indirectly. $HOME/.codex/hooks.json runs `ai-memory ... hook --event <session-start|user-prompt-submit|pre-tool-use|post-tool-use|stop|session-end> --server-url http://127.0.0.1:49374` for every Codex session, so the one sanctioned `codex exec --sandbox read-only --ephemeral` review (cwd = this worktree) most likely posted lifecycle observations to the live store; likewise the Claude worker session itself runs under $HOME/.claude/settings.json hooks that post to the same service. The unit made no direct ai-memory CLI/HTTP call and did not query the live store to check (the hard rule forbids calls to it), so whether those hooks created a live project/workspace for the worktree path is unverified and is left to the coordinator.
